review_notes:
I read the whole target file. I also read `sumPow` in ScalarBraiding.lean, `sumPowIns`/`sumPowPrj` in SuperEmbed/Standard.lean, and the `mixFun_inl` lemmas in MixShuffle.lean. I searched Mathlib's CategoryTheory for an existing iterated binary biproduct indexed by `Fin (k+1)` and found none. Mathlib's `biproduct` over `Fin (k+1)` is the canonical n-ary concept.

The mix-split declarations (`mixSplitHom`, `mixSplitInv`, `mixSplitIso`) are specific to `OddLine.mix` and are not duplicates. The only candidate is the `sumPow` representation that `constSumIso` bridges, and `sumPow` is defined outside this file.

Uncertainty: `sumPow` may have been chosen on purpose, because it needs only `HasBinaryBiproducts` and supports inductive proofs of `schurKilled_sumPow_*`. Moving those proofs to the n-ary biproduct would take real work. This file also adds `attribute [local instance] hasBinaryBiproducts_of_finite_biproducts`, so `HasFiniteBiproducts` is available wherever the bridge is used. I therefore rate the finding as moderate.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def constSumIso
    [Category.{v} D] [Preadditive D] [HasFiniteBiproducts D]
    (X : D) (k : ℕ) :
    (⨁ fun _ : Fin (k + 1) => X) ≅ sumPow X k where
findings.problem: The project defines its own `k+1`-fold biproduct of a single object, `sumPow`, as a left-nested binary `⊞`. That duplicates Mathlib's `⨁ fun _ : Fin (k+1) => X`. The copy comes with its own inclusion and projection family (`sumPowIns`, `sumPowPrj`), its own same/ne orthogonality lemmas and its own totality lemma (`sumPow_total`). These re-prove for the iterated binary sum what `biproduct.ι_π_self`, `biproduct.ι_π_ne` and `biproduct.lift_desc` already give. `constSumIso` exists only to convert between the two representations. It is used once, inside `mixSumPowIso`, which is needed only because the `schurKilled_sumPow_*` and `not_schurKilled_sum` results are stated for `sumPow`. Every consumer pays for the conversion.
findings.proposed_change: Prefer the existing `biproduct` representation. State `schurKilled_sumPow_unit`, `schurKilled_sumPow_odd` and `not_schurKilled_sum` for `⨁ fun _ : Fin (p+1) => 𝟙_ A` and `⨁ fun _ : Fin (q+1) => U`. Run the existing inductions through a one-step peeling iso, as MixShuffle already does for `mixSuccHom`. Then `constSumIso`, `sumPowIns`, `sumPowPrj` and the totality/orthogonality lemmas become unnecessary, and `mixSumPowIso` reduces to `mixSplitIso`. If `sumPow` must stay, document it as a proof-only device. Also reduce the API to `sumPow X k ≅ ⨁ fun _ : Fin (k+1) => X`, so that the n-ary biproduct is the one canonical object.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical representation of the constant finite biproduct, with Mathlib's lemma library available directly. Roughly 100 lines of bespoke insertion/projection API and the conversion isomorphism go away, and results stay compatible with other biproduct-indexed statements.
